name: Ferrante vaginal estrogen
question: Do vaginal estrogen ring or cream reduce six-month urinary tract infection recurrence versus placebo cream in postmenopausal women?

design.population: Postmenopausal women with documented recurrent urinary tract infection.
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Objectives, Methods, and Results

verdictNote: The active arms were pooled after slow recruitment; nine women withdrew before month six.
takeaway: In postmenopausal women with recurrent UTI, pooled vaginal estrogen ring or cream produced fewer six-month UTI endpoint failures than placebo cream (11/18 versus 16/17; P = 0.041), counting withdrawals as failures.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.dateLocator: Publisher article record, online-ahead-of-print note; print issue February 2021
reports.citation: Ferrante KL, Wasenda EJ, Jung CE, et al. "Vaginal Estrogen for the Prevention of Recurrent Urinary Tract Infection in Postmenopausal Women: A Randomized Clinical Trial." *Female Pelvic Med Reconstr Surg.* 2021;27(2):112-117. doi:10.1097/SPV.0000000000000749
reports.followUp: six-month randomized comparison, then optional six-month open-label estrogen

results.endpoint: Urinary tract infection by six months
results.measure: Intention-to-treat proportion with UTI endpoint failure; dropouts counted as failures
results.note: The abstract reports a P value but does not state the prespecified significance threshold.

results.endpoint: Urinary tract infection by six months among completers
results.note: Completer analysis after nine pre-six-month withdrawals.

delivery.label: Randomization and analysis
delivery.value: Initial 1:1:1 allocation to estrogen ring, estrogen cream, or placebo cream; active arms combined for comparison with placebo after slow recruitment.

delivery.label: Withdrawal before six months
delivery.note: Percentages calculated from the pooled analysis denominators.

relations.note: Both placebo-controlled trials found fewer recurrences with vaginal estrogen; Ferrante combined ring and cream arms.
Both found fewer recurrences with vaginal estrogen; Eriksen tested a ring against no estrogen treatment.
